Lane 1 — PR-SWEEP tracking: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13872

Scope: every open PR across developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber, dezren39/fleet not currently claimed/worked. Census in progress; progress posted on #13872 at every slice boundary.

Lane 7 (stray-work) tracking issue: #13874 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13874

Scope claim (Lane 7): stray-work labelling, parent/epic/design linkage and sub-issue trees for PRs/issues not tied to a design or roadmap item, hygiene pass over all open items + anything closed/active since 2026-10-23, across code / opencode / openchamber / fleet. Per the umbrella dedupe rule I will check item comments for lane claims before editing, and where lanes 2-4 own an item's primary scope I will record linkage findings as pointer comments here instead of editing the item.

Lane 6 — DESIGN-GAPS tracking: #13873 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13873

Scope: all designs + all issues demanding a design across code / opencode / openchamber / fleet; missing + deficient designs judged against the 9-point sufficient-design standard in #13873; prioritised gaps packetised to queue `repo-health-code-pilot` (kind `feature_slice` + `payload.slice`).

Lane 3 — OPEN-ISSUES-AUDIT — tracking issue: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13875

Scope: every open issue across developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber, dezren39/fleet — read fully, one by one. Labels/links/blocker legibility, blocker validity, mutual blocks, epic restructuring, decision/parked/blocked verification.

Status at filing: census fetch in progress via `fleet gh api --paginate` (fleet gh cache daemon is down — calls resolve in-process and are slow, ~2 min each, so this lane batches by repo). Progress will be posted on #13875 at every slice boundary.

Lane 2 (CLOSED-ISSUES-REVIEW, past month since 2026-10-23) tracking issue: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13878

Scope: every issue closed since 2026-10-23 in developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber, dezren39/fleet — read in full (body + comments), one by one. Census/dump in progress on the laptop via fleet gh; progress will be posted on #13878 at every slice boundary.

Coordination noted: label additions inside the closed-issue scope are Lane 2's (Lane 7 notified via this comment — no duplicate labelling); "closed but not actually implemented" cases will be pointed here for Lane 4 (PR side), reopen/correction decision stays with Lane 2.

AUDIT-7 Lane 5 (DESIGN-REVIEW) tracking issue: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13876

Lane 5 owns: internal soundness of every design record in doc/ + their tracking issues (gaps, dependency order, head prioritisation). Lane 6 owns sufficient-design-standard failures — pointers for those will be posted here, not duplicated.

Lane 4 — MERGED-PR-AUDIT tracking: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13879

Scope: every PR merged since 2026-10-23 across developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber, dezren39/fleet — read PR + diff in full, compared to its spawning issue (especially Closes/fixes closures); later-PR completions checked before any gap is filed. Outcome labels created in developing-today/code: audit:complete, audit:partial, audit:gap-filed, audit:bug-filed, audit:completed-later, audit:no-issue (definitions on #13879). Progress posted on #13879 at every slice boundary. Coordination: Lane 2 owns reopen/correction decisions on closures; Lane 4 owns the PR-vs-issue comparison and gap-filing — Lane 2 pointers on this umbrella will be prioritised for comparison.

Lane 4 pointer for Lane 2 (CLOSED-ISSUES-REVIEW) — suspect closure, dezren39/fleet#32:

fleet#32's body asks for a VISIBILITY fix ("an optional leg that errors should be impossible to miss in a green run — export.sh emits a workflow warning annotation and a step-summary table of per-leg outcomes; the smoke job lists which repos' closures the published image contains"). PR #8675 (`style(id/web): biome-format the nine files failing biome-check (#5302)`, merged 2026-11-11T12:49:23Z, labelled `audit:partial`) closed issue #5302 (main-broken: `id` workflow failed on main @464467b) 1 second after merge via its "Fixes #5302" keyword.

Why the closure looks suspect:
- #5302's failing run (41722852515) listed ~13 failing jobs, not one: biome-check, cargo-fmt-check, clippy-lint, crash-gate-sampled, prettier-check, rustfmt-check, test-shard-0, test-unit, treefmt-check, web-fmt-check, web-lint, native arm64 world-snapshot determinism. PR #8675 fixes only the biome-check slice (9 files, formatting only).
- The issue's own early triage notes say "This is not a single isolated biome-check issue" (cargo-fmt/clippy errors, web-lint diagnostics, three unit-test failures).
- The issue's acceptance requires the named workflow to complete green on a subsequent main commit (or the breakage shown superseded by a later green main run). No such verification is recorded on #5302: the PR body itself says "CI could not answer first (all recent `id` workflow runs on main are queued)", and no comment after the merge records a green main run.
- Sibling PRs the same day plausibly covered parts of the failure set (e.g. #8668 fixed the lib test-target compile break behind test-unit), but nothing on #5302 ties the full failure list to fixes or a green run.

Suggested Lane 2 check: confirm whether the `id` workflow went green on main after the 2026-11-11 sweep, and if any of run 41722852515's failures (notably clippy-lint, test-shard-0, world snapshot determinism) remained unaddressed, decide whether #5302 needs reopening or a follow-up issue.
